svg.title: Retatrutide sits on the drug side of FDA's 40-amino-acid line
svg.desc: Alpha-amino-acid count of each molecule's chain, by U.S. status. Over 40 counts as a protein, which is regulated as a biologic. TB-500 (Ac-LKKTETQ fragment): 7; BPC-157: 15; Liraglutide (Victoza, Saxenda): 31; Semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy): 31; Teriparatide (Forteo): 34; Cagrilintide (in CagriSema): 37; Pramlintide (Symlin): 37; Exenatide (Byetta): 39; Retatrutide: 39; Tirzepatide (Mounjaro, Zepbound): 39; Lixisenatide (Adlyxin, Soliqua): 44; Tesamorelin (Egrifta): 44; Insulin degludec (Tresiba): 50; Insulin human (Humulin R): 51. Every approved product at 40 or fewer is a drug; every one above 40 is a biologic.

text.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
